keyVerseText: And killed the Prince of life, whom God hath raised from the dead; whereof we are witnesses. Prince: or, Author
rootMeaning: The Greek word ἀρχηγός (archēgós) is formed from ἀρχή (archḗ), meaning 'beginning' or 'principle,' and ἄγω (ágō), meaning 'to lead.' Thus, its root meaning conveys the idea of one who leads from the beginning or who originates something. This literal sense enriches the common English glosses like 'author' or 'chief leader' by emphasizing both the role of origin and leadership—someone who initiates and guides.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, ἀρχηγός appears four times and is translated variously as 'the Prince,' 'to be a Prince,' 'the captain,' and 'the author.' This range shows the word’s flexibility in denoting a chief leader or originator, whether as a ruler, commander, or founder. The consistency in these translations highlights the word’s core meaning of primary leadership and foundational authority.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding ἀρχηγός as both 'author' and 'chief leader' is crucial for grasping Christ’s role in the New Testament. He is not only the initiator of salvation but also the supreme leader who guides His people. This dual aspect underscores the sovereignty and foundational nature of Christ’s work, affirming His divine authority as the source and pioneer of life and faith. Recognizing this enriches our faith by anchoring it in Christ’s unique position as the originator and ruler over all things.
keyVerseReflection: Acts 3:15 declares Jesus as 'the Prince of life, whom God hath raised from the dead,' with an alternate reading of 'Author.' Here, ἀρχηγός conveys both His preeminence as the sovereign leader over life and His role as the originator of eternal life itself. This word choice powerfully affirms that Jesus is the source and ruler of life, reinforcing the witness of the apostles to His resurrection and divine authority.
